name: GAFNet
description: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) affects 5–7% of school-age children globally, yet reliable objective diagnosis is absent from routine clinical practice. Electroencephalography (EEG) offers a cost-accessible, millisecond-resolution window into neural dynamics; however, existing deep-learning models are evaluated on single datasets, rarely discriminate among ADHD subtypes, and neglect the non-Euclidean topology of electrode networks. This paper proposes GAFNet (Graph-Augmented Fusion Network), addressing three concur-rent limitations through: (i) a Graph-Augmented Transformer (GAF) encoder that embeds PLV-derived spatial graphs directly into multi-head self-attention; (ii) a Cross-Modal Attention Gate (CMAG) that learns frequency-band × brain-region co-activation signatures; and (iii) a Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD) domain-adaptation loss that reduces cross-dataset distributional divergence by 81.5%, enabling unified training across the heterogeneous Nasrabadi 2020 (19-channel, 121 subjects, resting-state) and Vahid 2019 (19-channel, 144 subjects, event-related) benchmarks. GAFNet attains 99.1±0.28% accuracy (AUC 0.998; 99.2% aggregate out-of-fold) on binary ADHD/HC classification and 88.7 ± 2.1% accuracy (AUC 0.923; 88.9% aggregate) on three-class subtype classification (ADD vs. ADHD-C vs. HC), with significance confirmed via a corrected resampled test (p < 0.01) against all baselines. The Nasrabadi component is fully reproducible from public data; the Vahid component is reproducible subject to a data-use request to the original authors.
